subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this crash-loop by landing the fixed 8192 MB managed-service heap default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, require a tunable heap surface first, or stay with the existing wrapper-only path?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing a default heap cap affects fresh installs and forced reinstalls across host sizes and intersects the intentional `NODE_OPTIONS` security boundary.

options.title: Accept fixed emergency default
options.body: Land the heap-only generated service default now to mitigate the reported crash loop, and track any configurable heap surface separately.

options.title: Require tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the active PR until maintainers choose a CLI/config/doctor surface with upgrade proof for low-memory and fleet-managed hosts.

options.title: Keep wrapper-only policy
options.body: Reject a generated default and rely on the documented `--wrapper` path for operators who need custom Node startup flags.

recommendation.title: Accept fixed emergency default
recommendation.body: Land the heap-only generated service default now to mitigate the reported crash loop, and track any configurable heap surface separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has recent daemon helper history and was explicitly pulled into the issue discussion for this managed-service behavior decision.
